machine.shared: A development machine, at rest for this study: every round ran under the lock of the measurements; the two agents of the machine, a logcenter and three gates of an application stayed up, idle

build.tls: OpenSSL 3.6.5 (bundled, static: linux-ext-libs 1.31 on both sides); mbedTLS not built on this machine
build.note: CONFIG_DEBUG_TRACK_MEMORY is on (the .config of this machine): every allocation is tracked. A build without it does less work per allocation; that build was not measured here.

method.ab: Written on 2026-11-25, before the tag. 7.32.3 is the C code of a0aa4d8b2, its version commit, measured against 7.32.0, the last release with a study. 7.32.1 and 7.32.2 changed no C of the libraries or the yunos (a test of timeranger2, and the `ylabel` command), so they are inside it. The one C change is in root-linux: C_CHANNEL counts its connections and C_IDP_KEYCLOAK drops an answer whose requester is gone. Of the objects of the SDK only c_channel.c.o and c_idp_keycloak.c.o have other machine code. Both sides are git worktrees (yunetas-perf-head at 318204992 and yunetas-perf-7.32.3) built by `yunetas init --sdk-only` and `make install` of the kernel libraries and modules into their own outputs/, the benchmarks and the three ctest binaries from their root build/, the yunos by make; linux-ext-libs 1.31 on both sides. the binaries pinned to one CPU (taskset -c 6) and run in rotation, the order turned each round, a sync and a 3 s pause (1 s for the three ctest binaries) before each run: 10 rounds. Mean +- standard deviation (median), t = the change over its standard error; |t| < 3 is noise. The two figures outside their noise (both faster, both of the mask) were measured again, 10 more rounds of their benchmark (perf_micro); their reasons give both runs. The three appends of the rkey phase of perf_timeranger2, new in 7.32.0, have their first A/B here. The BFF figure and the event loop echoes are means of the samples of a run, the first left out (and the last, for the echoes). The treedb figures (perf_tr_treedb, perf_tr_treedb_read) are CPU time of the process; perf_c_treedb is wall time. The page-by-page read rate is the mean of the FORWARD and BACKWARD passes of test_topic_pkey_integer_iterator5. perf_http and perf_micro are the drivers written for the 7.31.0 study, kept since. No hardware counters (perf_event_paranoid is 4 on this machine and no root). The rounds ran with the machine at rest, a load average of 1 to 1.6.
method.tag_run: The absolute figures of 7.32.3 are its side of the A/B run (a0aa4d8b2, its version commit), measured on 2026-11-25. The binary sizes are those of the yunos of that worktree, built with the same .config (make, not installed).

story.title: Yuneta 7.32.3 against 7.32.0
story.lead: 7.32.3 sends the answer of an IdP command to the connection that asked, or to nobody: C_CHANNEL counts its connections, and C_IDP_KEYCLOAK drops an answer whose channel closed or holds another connection. It is the only C change, in two objects of root-linux. Measured against 7.32.0 before the tag: all 69 figures inside their noise.

hero.text: figures inside their noise against 7.32.0: two objects changed (c_channel.c.o and c_idp_keycloak.c.o), and the two figures of the mask that left their noise in the first ten rounds are inside it over twenty.

tiles: Records read per second, page by page
treedb: update a node and save it
story.ab_sub: Each benchmark built from the tree of each release (7.32.0 and 7.32.3), pinned to one CPU, the binaries run in rotation: 10 rounds. A change inside its whisker is noise.
story.abs_sub: Absolute figures of the 7.32.3 build (a0aa4d8b2, its version commit), measured on 2026-11-25 on the laptop above, as its side of the A/B run: one process, pinned to one CPU. Mean of the 10 rounds.
story.no_prices: No figure is slower outside its noise: there is no price to name in this release.
